newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end sluggish day lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end sluggish day lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished a sluggish session with fairly large losses, pressured by sentiment that gains in recent weeks had left the market overbought.
Weakness in the bond market also fueled selling in early dealings, but a recovery in bonds in afternoon trade had little impact on futures.

"Bonds came charging back to the plus side and we were languishing," said Kevin O'Brien, stock index futures analyst on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange floor for Prudential Securities. "That worries me."
However, in order for the bearish tone to remain intact, O'Brien said the September S&P 500 contract would have needed to close below 898.00. September S&Ps closed at 899.30.
In fact, the September contract rallied in afternoon dealings to reach a new session high but quickly came off as selling resumed, hovering near midrange the remainder of the session.
With the uncertain outlook in the near term, one S&P trader said the contract high of 908.50 in September S&Ps is likely to hold "for the next couple of days, if not for the next couple of weeks."
Prices are likely to remain rangebound as the so-called triple expiration, which sometimes lead to choppy trading conditions, begins tomorrow at the close, .
June contracts in stock index futures, options and individual equity options begin their expirations at the close Thursday and finish at the close Friday.

Traders said there has been little talk of a directional bias to the expiration, other than the seasonal-type upward bias that has been associated in the two weeks surrounding the last several quarterly expirations.
